book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Second Level; 15. Trolls’ Chamber
text: Six troll guards nest in this room. Two of them keep watch in the northern passage (within the area marked by Xs) and two others do the same in the southern passage. The other two monsters are in the central chamber. Dozens of various polearms, morningstars, and swords lie heaped in the middle of the room. (These are used to arm the gnolls currently penned in areas 16 and 17.)

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Second Level; 16. Thrall Pen
text: Sixteen unarmed gnolls dwell here. Each has nothing but a heap of straw and a hide coverlet. Although these creatures are enslaved by the giants, they identify with their masters’ cause and will never help humans for any reason—in fact, they will gladly take up arms to fight intruders if given the chance.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Second Level; 17. Thrall Pen
text: Ten unarmed gnolls dwell here. They will behave in all respects like their kin in area 16.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 1. Cavern
text: This cavern is fairly colorful, having many reddish, pale yellow, and shining blue-gray rock formations that glisten in the light of torches or lanterns. Three ropers dwell here and conceal themselves among the natural stalagmite formations. They wait until prey approaches the center of the area before attacking.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 2. Glowing Cave
text: This small offshoot of the larger cavern that runs north and south is filled with luminous plant growth and contains twelve hungry giant fire beetles. Some will be on the ceiling and drop upon any creatures entering their lair. These creatures served as a source of gifts for the frost giants in the past. They have no treasure.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 4. Cave
text: Four hell hounds are on guard here, immediately giving voice if they detect any intruders.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 5. Cavern
text: Two fire giants are stationed here as a reserve on Snurre’s order (acting on instructions from the drow, of course). One rests in the northeast end while the other keeps watch, patrolling between the spots marked G. Each has several rocks nearby for throwing. They have a typical giant’s bag apiece, and the room also has piles of hides for bedding, a hamper or two, and some personal gear.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 6. Great Vaulted Cavern
text: In the middle of this place is a permanent illusion of a huge red dragon dozing atop a mound of treasure (appearing like area 7, below). What is actually in that spot is a gorgon that obeys drow and has been instructed to ignore the presence of such creatures as hell hounds and fire giants and trolls. If any other kind of creature speaks to it from a distance in Common or Draconic, it has been instructed to stand quietly but then to breathe upon intruders as soon as they are within range. The illusion disappears once the gorgon attacks.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 7. Treasure Trove Cave
text: This room is actually an extradimensional space, ten times larger than shown on the map. Anyone entering will notice first the enormous pile of treasure that fills the central part of the area and second the adult red dragon sleeping upon it.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 8. Cave
text: This is a drow guardroom, currently housing three drow elite warriors and six drow. All are clothed in black capes, shod with soft boots of black hide, and wear hoods over their helmets. Two sentries are on duty at all times near the entrance. The room holds only bedrolls and some miscellaneous gear.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 9. Wide Passage
text: Twelve piercers make their home in a cul de sac, where they patiently await unwary prey. The floor of the place is strewn with shattered skulls and bones.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 10. Singing Chamber
text: This small place has excellent acoustics, and the drops of water falling into the pool along the southern portion of the wall make a faint, pleasant musical sound that can be heard for 120 feet in silence (or from 60 feet away in normal conditions). The pool’s edge is lined by a huge patch of gray ooze, and another lies along a ledge 11 feet high in the southeast of the place.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 11–13. Stinking Caverns; 11. Troll Annex
text: Three trolls lounge herein, each with the typical messy mound of sticks and bones and other noisome things.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 11–13. Stinking Caverns; 12. Troll Central
text: Two trolls. This room, and its inhabitants, are much the same as those in area 11.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 11–13. Stinking Caverns; 13. Troll Heaven
text: Four trolls, including a dominant one that is particularly large (120 hit points), reside here. Conditions are similar to those in areas 11 and 12, except even more noisome.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 15. Gray Cavern
text: This dark-walled place is the drow strong point, and a drow watches each of the six routes that meet at this cavern. Four more drow are stationed in the chamber itself, for a total of ten.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 15. Gray Cavern
text: In addition, the eastern alcove serves as a field headquarters for two drow elite warriors (the female is in command) and a drow mage. Near this alcove, a narrow passage leads east and then south, ending at a set of rough-hewn stairs that ascend to the second level, emerging near area 8 on map 6.6.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 16. Small Cavern
text: There are nine female drow in the place. Five are normal drow, and three others are drow elite warriors. These eight guards protect Nedylene, a drow priestess of Lolth who is opposed to anything Eclavdra attempts. She is here to check up on her rival, and she will be suspicious of any creature entering her current abode. On the other hand, she will not be averse to seeing her rival’s plans go wrong, so negotiation is a possibility.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 17. Jeweled Cavern
text: If light strikes the walls of this cavern, mineral deposits make the place glitter and sparkle as if it were sown with jewels. This breathtakingly beautiful place is the current lair of two mind flayers who have decided to see what is going on with their friendly enemies, the drow. They plan to observe events, and the dark elves ignore them.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 18. Small Cavern
text: The cave at the end of the passage to the northeast is another drow guardroom, with occupants and contents identical to area 8: three drow elite warriors and six drow, two of which are on duty at all times near the entrance.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 19. Salamander Central
text: Amid this vaporous inferno in the area to the southeast are two salamanders enjoying a change of clime. The flames and smoke render the area lightly obscured. The salamanders are totally indifferent with respect to whom they attack, although they know and respect the drow.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Against the Giants; Hall of the Fire Giant King; Locations on the Third Level; 20. Council Chamber and Drow HQ
text: Currently in this place (at the least) are six drow and four drow elite warriors, one of which is a female commander who has 110 hit points. The commander has a +2 shortsword, a +1 hand crossbow, and three magic bolts, as follows:

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Running the Adventure; Adventure Start
text: On a roll of 1 to 16, no demon appears. Otherwise the following demons could appear: 17, a vrock; 18, a hezrou; 19, a glabrezu; or 20, a nalfeshnee.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 8. Gargoyle Lair
text: Creature. A mutated, four-armed gargoyle attacks anyone who enters its lair. This creature uses Multiattack to make three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 13. Chamber of Three Chests
text: Gold. Opening the gold chest releases a swarm of poisonous snakes that slither out and attack next round. They continue biting until all are killed.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 13. Chamber of Three Chests
text: Oak. When the lid of the oak chest is opened, an animated giant skeleton (see appendix B) will be instantly teleported into the room, and it strikes with surprise.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 18. Corridor Protected by Fear Gas; 18A. False Crypt
text: Creature. The false crypt is the home of a false lich that is actually a magically prepared greater zombie (see appendix B). Between strikes the creature will gesture with its hands as if readying a spell. If it is struck by the golden mace it will make a roaring bellow (produced by a magic mouth spell), and the weapon will obviously stagger it (roll dice and shake your head ruefully) every time the mace is used. The third time it is struck by the glowing mace, the false lich will instantly wither and disappear in a puff of dust, and the mace will shatter.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 19. Laboratory and Mummy Preparation Room
text: The eastern vat contains a grayish substance that is actually an ochre jelly that sits atop the other half of the golden key.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 21. The Agitated Chamber
text: Treasure. The trunks are empty, but the smaller coffers hold various items. Roll a d6 each time one is opened. On a roll of 1–3, the coffer contains 1d3 poisonous snakes. On a roll of 4–5, 8d10 pp are found. On a roll of 6, the coffer holds 2d4 gems (worth 10 gp each).

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 22. The Cavern of Gold and Silver Mists
text: Creature. At the center of the cavern is a small grotto in which dwells the fey being Siren (see appendix B). As a private joke, Acererak placed her in this cavern under an enchantment. She must be asked to come out of the chamber in order to break the spell, and she can give no clues as to the nature of her durance. If the characters come close enough, they can see that two sacks, a large one and a small one, are lying on the floor next to her.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 25. Pillared Throne Room
text: Treasure. Each of these items is obviously valuable (25,000 gp for the crown, 12,500 gp for the scepter), but both are cursed. If they are removed from the tomb, the possessor of either item will be visited by a vrock sent to reclaim the item and return it to the throne room—or by two such demons if a single character has both items.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 26. Small Room with a Door of Electric Blue
text: Creature. The gem has an evil magic placed upon it, and if it is removed from the mummy, the remains become a true mummy lord that has no spells and no legendary actions (defeating it awards half XP). Magic upon the mummy lord’s wrappings makes them nonflammable, and the creature wears a ring of resistance (fire).

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 27. The Portal of Scintillating Violet
text: Creatures. If the threshold of the chamber is crossed by any creature, one set of swords will fly off the wall and attack the individual so doing. The two flying swords will both attack, and the shield (statistics as the swords, but no attacks) will interpose itself to take hits meant for the swords. This trio will attack until they are destroyed or the one who violated their area is dead. Surviving weapons and shields return to their former positions after the offender is hacked to pieces.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 29. The Valves of Mithral
text: Levitate coagulates the blood and causes it to rise up as a Huge red ochre jelly.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 29. The Valves of Mithral
text: Polymorph changes the blood into seven wights, which attack immediately.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 30. False Treasure Room
text: Bronze Urn. A character who examines the urn can use an action to pry loose the stopper. If the stopper is removed, an efreeti will come forth. If the urn has been battered, knocked about, shaken, overturned, or otherwise roughly handled, the creature will be in a fury and will attack. If not, it will grant three wishes for the party and then depart.

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 33. The Crypt of Acererak the Demilich
text: All that now remains of Acererak the lich are the dust of his bones. This bit is enough! If any of the treasure in the crypt is touched, the dust swirls into the air and forms a man-like shape. If this shape is ignored, it will dissipate in 3 rounds, for it can only advance and threaten, not harm. Any physical attack will give it 1 point of energy, however, and a damaging spell cast on it gives it a number of points of energy equal to the level of the spell slot expended (1 point for a cantrip). Each point of energy is equivalent to a hit point, and if 50 hit points are thus gained, the dust will form into a ghost controlled by Acererak, and this thing will attack immediately. (The dust will seem to waver and fall back if it is struck by blow or spell, as if suffering actual damage, so formation of the ghost isn’t too improbable.)

book_path: Tales from the Yawning Portal; Tomb of Horrors; Locations in the Tomb; 33. The Crypt of Acererak the Demilich
text: If any character is so foolish as to touch the skull of the demilich, a terrible thing occurs. Acererak rises into the air upon the touch, and it slowly scans the party prior to attacking. The demilich has the Trap the Soul action and access to its lair actions, but not lair traits. It can tell which members of the party are the most powerful, and it uses Trap the Soul on them first.
